messages.author: 556685e17a412579
messages.subject: Solving the Error in drawParam
parts:
Hi,

I am working on a Power Analysis helping one professor of mine. I follow the tutorial from the Donnelly et al.
We have run a preliminary study, we have collected some standardized betas and we now use them in the model to find based on the them the sample we need for a power above 80%.

Our model is a moderated mediation one (similar to the one reported in the paper). Yet, when we put our parameters instead of those in the paper we receive the "Error in draw Param".
 
At some point Pr. Jorgensen mentioned in another discussion: "If you are getting that drawParam() error, perhaps you need to specify standardized parameters more carefully.  The tutorial shows how to use the simsem::find*() functions to find the residual variance that would make the total variance 1.  Making sure your explained variance is not > 1 can prevent the drawParam() error."

Yet, I am not sure how to use it. The code I have is for simplicity the same as Donnelly et al., (with just some different names)

N.per.group <- 25 # balanced group sample sizes
designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = 1:0, W = 1:0)
designMatrix$XW <- designMatrix$X * designMatrix$W # interaction
exoData <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:N.per.group, function(i)designMatrix))
a.w0 <- .5 # effect of X on M when moderator (W) == 0
 a.mod <- .3 # how much "a" path is moderated by W (i.e., interaction)
 b.w0 <- .4 # effect of M on Y when moderator (W) == 0
b.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on "b" path
 c.w0 <- .2 # effect of X on Y when moderator (W) == 0
c.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on "c" path
 w.M <- .1 # simple effect of moderator (W) on M when X == 0
 w.Y <- -.1 # simple effect of moderator (W) on Y when X == 0
 kappa.free <- kappa.pop <- matrix(NA, # estimate all effects
      nrow = 2, # 2 outcomes (M and Y)
      ncol = 3, # dummy coded X, W, XW
      dimnames = list(c("M","Y"),
      names(exoData)))
kappa.free["M","X"] <- "a.w0" # label free parameters
kappa.free["M","W"] <- "w.M" # (to define indirect effects)
kappa.free["M","XW"] <- "a.mod"
kappa.free["Y","X"] <- "c.w0"
kappa.free["Y","W" "w.Y"
kappa.free["Y","XW"] <- 0 # fixed to 0; label “c.mod” to free

kappa.pop["M","X"] <- a.w0 # set population parameters
kappa.pop["M","W"] <- w.M # (defined above)
kappa.pop["M","XW"] <- a.mod
kappa.pop["Y","X"] <- c.w0
kappa.pop["Y","W"] <- w.Y
kappa.pop["Y","XW"] <- c.mod

exoPaths <- bind(free = kappa.free, popParam = kappa.pop)

beta.free <- beta.pop <- matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = 2,
        dimnames = list(c("M","Y"), c("M","Y")))
beta.free["Y", "M"] <- "b"
beta.pop["Y", "M"] <- b.w0

endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)

residCor <- binds(free = diag(as.numeric(NA), 2), popParam = diag(2))

userParams <- ' ## conditional indirect effects
ind.w0 := a.w0 * b
ind.w1 := (a.w0 + a.mod) * b
## Test H0: equivalent indirect effects across W
ind.diff := a.mod * b
## or equivalently:
# ind.diff := ind.w1 – ind.w0 '

modMed1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor,
                       KA = exoPaths, con = userParams, indLab = rownames(kappa.free),
                       covLab = colnames(kappa.free))
sim1 <- sim(nRep = 100, model = modMed1, covData = exoData,
                        n = nrow(exoData), seed = 777, outfun = rejectMCCI,
                        meanstructure = FALSE) # pass this argument to lavaan

set.seed(355)
 datmod <- generate(modMed1, covData = exoData, n = nrow(exoData))

Thank you in advance for any comment or help.
Best,
JP

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Solving the Error in drawParam
parts: I run the code and I receive the population diagonal as a NA diagonal.

No you don't.  You receive these population values, which you pass to the popParam= argument of binds():

> resVars
[1] 0.9375 0.8100
 
The NA values are what you pass to the free= argument of binds(), indicating those residual variances are free parameters in the analysis (not population) model.
The problem is I do not get how find function works to make the relevant change.
You used it correctly in your example.  The resVars object contains the residual variances that make the model-implied total variances = 1 in the population.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
